scientific_queries.note: Data-based verification of pool labels plus the genuine both-drugs-unseen head-to-head.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round verifies its own labels by data rather than by reading code, then closes the last untested comparison.
key_detail: the constant marginal baseline scores 0.63%, BELOW random at 1.25%, because tie-breaking takes the first k rows; so beating it is not evidence of skill and random is the correct reference

complete_picture.both_drugs_seen: model loses to marginals by 3.75 pp and does not beat random
complete_picture.one_drug_unseen: model beats random by 3.25 pp but loses to marginals (not significantly)
complete_picture.both_drugs_unseen: model does not establish a gain over random (+1.25 pp, CI includes 0) even though it is the only predictor with information there

conclusion: in no pool does the annotation model both beat random significantly AND beat the marginal baseline
limits: the both-unseen pool holds about 1,830 keys, so its CI is wide and 'not established' is not 'zero'
the constant baseline's tie-breaking is arbitrary, which is why random is used as the reference
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: the annotation line has now been tested in three information regimes with consistent results; further variants add little without finer features or a new resource
